However, both Greene's character and personality are actually based on Bugsy Siegel: his affiliation with the mob in Los Angeles, his involvement in the development of Las Vegas, and his flamboyant tendencies.  Greene is portrayed in the movie by Alex Rocco.
Moe's (bar and lounge) | Moe's was a popular bar in Fort Greene, Brooklyn named after the tavern that appears in "The Simpsons" owned and run by the character Moe Szyslak.

Carlo Tramonti | Carlo Tramonti is a fictional character in the novels "The Godfather" and "The Godfather's Revenge".  In the universe of the novels, he is the Don of the Tramonti crime family (inspired of New Orleans crime family) from 1931 to 1964.

Władysław Moes | Władysław Gerard Jan Nepomuk Marya Moes (17 November 1900 – 17 December 1986 ) was a Polish aristocrat and has been claimed as the inspiration for the character Tadzio in Thomas Mann’s novella "Death in Venice".
Carmine Marino | Carmine Marino is a fictional character who plays a prominent role in the novel "The Godfather Returns" and in its sequel, "The Godfather's Revenge".

Alex Rocco | Alessandro Federico Petricone, Jr. (February 29, 1936 – July 18, 2015), known professionally as Alex Rocco, was an American actor.  Often cast as a villain, he is best known for his portrayal of Moe Greene in "The Godfather" and his Primetime Emmy Award for Supporting Actor in a Comedy for "The Famous Teddy Z".  He did a significant amount of voiceover work later in his career, and was known for his gravelly voice.  He was also a member of the Bahá'í Faith.

Vito Corleone | Vito Corleone is a fictional character in Mario Puzo's novel "The Godfather" and in the first two of Francis Ford Coppola's three Godfather films, in which he was portrayed by Marlon Brando in "The Godfather" and then, as a young man, by Robert De Niro in "The Godfather Part II".  He is an orphaned Sicilian immigrant who builds a mafia empire.  Upon his death, Michael, his youngest son, succeeds him as the mafia don of the Corleone crime family.

Emilio Barzini | Emilio "The Wolf" Barzini is a fictional character and one of the primary antagonists, alongside with Virgil Sollozzo, in Mario Puzo's novel "The Godfather" and in its film adaptation, in which he is portrayed by Richard Conte.  The Barzini crime family was inspired by the Genovese crime family.
Tommy Neri | Thomas 'Tommy' Neri is a fictional character in the novels "The Godfather, The Godfather Returns", and "The Godfather's Revenge".
Lucy Mancini | Lucy Mancini is a fictional character in Mario Puzo's "The Godfather".  She was portrayed by Jeannie Linero in "The Godfather" and "The Godfather Part III".
prediction.summary_1: Moe Dalitz, an American gangster, businessman, casino owner, and philanthropist, was a close associate of Hyman "Pittsburgh Hymie" Martin. His name served as one of the inspirations for the fictional character "Moe Greene" in Mario Puzo's "The Godfather."
prediction.summary_2: While Moe Dalitz was a real-life American gangster and businessman who contributed to the development of Las Vegas, the claim that he was the primary inspiration for the character Moe Greene in "The Godfather" is only partially accurate. The name "Moe Greene" is a composite of several real-life mobsters, including Dalitz, Moe Sedway, and Gus Greenbaum; however, the character's personality and life story are primarily modeled after Bugsy Siegel.
